unit.title: Promote and up-sell products and services

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is up-selling?
options: Offering a better, dearer choice of what they want
Selling the guest something they never asked about at all
Lowering the price so the guest buys more items
Selling the property's goods to another hotel

questions.stem: A guest orders jerk chicken. The server suggests a side of festival and a sorrel drink to go with it. What is this called?
options: Up-selling
Cross-selling
Discounting
Complaint handling

questions.stem: Why do properties want their staff to promote and up-sell?
options: So guests spend money on things they do not need
So staff can earn more tips than the managers
To raise sales and help guests enjoy their stay
To use up old stock before it goes out of date

questions.stem: Why must you know the property's products, prices and opening times well?
options: So you can tell guests what other hotels charge
So you can change the prices if a guest asks
So you can avoid speaking to guests about them
So you can advise guests correctly

questions.stem: At an all-inclusive resort, a guest asks if a spa massage is in the package. You are not sure. What should you do?
options: Say yes, so the guest books the massage
Say no, so the guest pays for it later
Check the package details, then tell the guest
Tell the guest to ask at reception tomorrow morning

questions.stem: What is the best way to find out what a guest might like?
options: Guess from the clothes and shoes they are wearing
Ask open questions and listen to the answers
Read their private booking notes aloud
Tell them what you would choose yourself

questions.stem: Which of these is an open question?
options: What sort of day trip would you enjoy most?
Would you like to book a day trip with us?
Do you want to book the river rafting trip?
Is the beach trip all right for you today?

questions.stem: A couple tell the front desk they are on honeymoon. Which suggestion fits them best?
options: A private sunset dinner on the beach
The children's club and kids' menu
A business centre printing package
A group bus tour with a school party

questions.stem: A family with two small children asks about things to do at the property. What could you suggest?
options: The late-night adults-only bar party
A conference room for a business meeting
The kids' club and a family pool day
A wine-tasting evening for couples

questions.stem: Which sentence turns a feature of an ocean-view room into a benefit for the guest?
options: The room is on the fourth floor of the main block
The room has a large balcony with two chairs
You can watch the sunset from your own balcony
The room costs a little more than a garden-view room

questions.stem: What is a "feature" of a product?
options: What the guest gains from using it
The reason the guest gives for saying no
The cost of the product, including GCT
A fact about it, such as its size

questions.stem: When is a good time to suggest dessert to a table?
options: When the main course plates are cleared
Before the guests have looked at the menu
While the guests are paying the bill
As soon as the guests sit down

questions.stem: When is a good time to offer a room upgrade to an arriving guest?
options: After they have unpacked in their first room
On the morning they leave the property
At check-in, before the key is given
In the middle of the night by phone

questions.stem: Which way of suggesting a drink is most likely to make a sale, without pressure?
options: "You don't want anything else, do you?"
"Drinks are over there if you want one."
"Would you like to try our fresh sorrel or a fruit punch?"
"Everybody else is having a cocktail, so you should too."

questions.stem: Why does a server describe a dish in an appetising way, for example "slow-cooked oxtail with butter beans"?
options: It helps the guest picture the dish and want it
It makes the dish take less time to cook
It means the price can be left off the menu
It stops guests from asking about allergens or spice

questions.stem: Why is it good to offer a guest a choice of two items, for example "the mango or the coconut cheesecake"?
options: It forces the guest to buy both items
It makes it easy for the guest to choose
It means you do not need to know the menu
It hides the price of the dearer item

questions.stem: Which body language helps when you promote a product to a guest?
options: Arms folded and looking at your phone
A smile, eye contact and an open posture
Standing very close and touching their arm
Looking at the floor and speaking quietly

questions.stem: A guest says the spa package is too expensive. What is a good response?
options: Tell them it is cheap and they are wrong
Walk away and serve another guest
Lower the price yourself without asking
Listen, then offer a smaller treatment

questions.stem: A guest politely says "No, thank you" to a tour you suggested. What should you do?
options: Thank them and accept their answer
Keep asking until they agree to go
Tell them they will regret it later
Offer the tour again each time you see them

questions.stem: Why must you never promise a guest something the property cannot deliver?
options: Because the guest will forget about it anyway
Because promises take too long to write down
Because other staff will want the same sale
It breaks trust and leads to complaints

questions.stem: A guest who looks about 16 asks for a rum punch at the pool bar. What should you do?
options: Serve it, as long as their parents are near
Serve a small one with extra juice in it
Charge the drink to their parents' room
Ask for ID and offer a non-alcoholic drink

questions.stem: A guest at the bar is clearly drunk and asks for a double. What should you do?
options: Up-sell them to a triple at a special price
Serve the drink quickly so that they will leave sooner
Politely refuse and offer water or a soft drink
Serve it but charge to another guest's room

questions.stem: A guest with a nut allergy wants to try the rum cake you suggested. What should you do?
options: Check the ingredients with the kitchen first
Say it is fine, because rum cake never has any nuts
Tell them to pick the nuts out themselves
Suggest a smaller slice so it will be safe

questions.stem: Which of these is a promotional item often placed on restaurant tables?
options: A guest registration card
A table tent card
A housekeeping checklist
A fire evacuation plan

questions.stem: A poster for Friday's jerk night still shows last month's prices. What should you do?
options: Leave it, as guests rarely read posters
Tell your supervisor so it can be updated
Cross out the prices with a marker pen
Charge guests the old prices without telling anyone

questions.stem: Why should brochures and displays be kept tidy and up to date?
options: So they can be thrown away less often
So staff do not need to learn the products
So they give guests a true, good picture
So guests do not ask any questions about them

questions.stem: You want to post a photo of the property's new cocktail on your own social media page. What should you do first?
options: Post it at once with the guests' faces in it
Check the property's social media rules
Add a lower price to bring in more people
Tag every guest who is staying at the property

questions.stem: A guest at the bar mentions that tomorrow is their wedding anniversary. What could you do to help service and sales?
options: Keep it to yourself, as it is private
Pass it on so the team can plan a treat
Tell the other guests at the bar
Charge the guest for an anniversary fee

questions.stem: A guest asks where to buy genuine Jamaican crafts. What is the best advice?
options: The gift shop or a licensed craft market
Tell them crafts are only sold at the airport
Send them to someone selling on the beach
Say you do not know and walk away

questions.stem: Why should you only recommend tours run by licensed operators?
options: Because they always cost the least money
Because the guest can then skip paying GCT
Because licensed tours never need booking
Because they meet safety standards

questions.stem: What is a "package" in hotel sales?
options: A box used to post items to guests in their home country
A discount given only to staff members
The luggage a guest brings with them
Several products sold together at one price

questions.stem: The restaurant has a Sunday brunch offer. How should you tell guests about it?
options: Only if they complain about the dinner menu
Mention it at the right time, with the main details
Hand out flyers to every guest at the pool, many times a day
Wait for guests to find it on the notice board

questions.stem: A guest asks the price of a spa treatment. What should you tell them?
options: A rough guess, to be fixed later at the spa
Only the price before GCT, so it sounds cheaper
The price another spa nearby charges
The correct price, and whether GCT is included

questions.stem: Why do some properties ask staff to record the extra sales they make?
options: So staff can be blamed for slow days
So guests can see who sold them what
To track results and see what works
To work out how much GCT each guest pays

questions.stem: After a week of promoting a new cocktail, very few have been sold. What is a sensible next step?
options: Ask guests and staff for feedback and change the approach
Stop telling guests about any drinks at all
Make guests buy one before they can order food
Blame the bar staff for not selling hard enough

questions.stem: Why does good service make it easier to promote and up-sell?
options: Because guests then forget to check the bill
Because good service means prices can be higher
Because staff do not need product knowledge
Because guests trust staff who treat them well

questions.stem: A guest checking in says they are celebrating a birthday. Which offer is suitable?
options: A move to a room beside the lift and ice machine
A discount on a late check-out next year
A copy of the menu from the staff canteen
A cake or a room upgrade, at the property's price

questions.stem: A guest orders "a coffee". How could you up-sell?
options: Bring a large one and charge for it without asking
Tell them coffee is bad for them
Say the coffee machine is broken
Offer a local speciality coffee or a large size

questions.stem: A guest asks you to suggest a Jamaican dish to try. Which answer shows good product knowledge?
options: "All the food here is much the same."
"Try the ackee and saltfish with fried dumpling."
"I only eat at home, so I would not know."
"Ask the chef, I do not work in the kitchen."

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign of pushy, unwanted selling?
options: Repeating an offer after the guest says no
Telling a guest the hours of the spa
Mentioning tonight's special once
Showing a guest the dessert menu

questions.stem: You are asked to plan a small promotion for the bar's happy hour. What should you decide first?
options: Who the guests are and what they would like
Which staff will get the day off
How to keep the real prices hidden from the guests
What colour the bar stools should be

questions.stem: Which is the most important information on a poster for a promotion?
options: The names of all the bar staff
What it is, when it is on and the price
The phone numbers of the suppliers
A long story about the history of Jamaican rum

questions.stem: Why must the description of a product on a menu or poster be true?
options: So the poster can be used for many years
So the kitchen can change the dish freely
So guests are not misled when they buy
So the price can be raised later on

questions.stem: A guest booked a tour you suggested and came back unhappy because it was not as you described. What should you do?
options: Tell them it is the tour company's fault only
Avoid the guest for the rest of their stay
Offer them a different tour at a higher price
Listen, apologise and tell your supervisor

questions.stem: What is Team Jamaica?
options: The national football team's fan club
A group of hotels that share guests
TPDCo training for people who work with visitors
A tour company that runs river trips

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

essays.stem: Explain the difference between up-selling and cross-selling, and give one example of each from a hotel or villa.
essays.modelAnswer: Up-selling means suggesting a better or larger version of what the guest has already chosen, so the sale is worth more. For example, a guest books a garden-view room and the front desk agent offers an ocean-view room with a balcony for a small extra charge, explaining that the guest can watch the sunset from it. Cross-selling means suggesting a different product that goes well with what the guest is buying. For example, a guest orders jerk pork in the restaurant and the server suggests a side of festival and a glass of fresh sorrel. Both raise sales, but both must be done to help the guest enjoy the stay, not to pressure them. The guest should always feel free to say no.
markingPoints: Up-selling: a better or larger version of the same item
A correct hotel or villa example of up-selling
Cross-selling: a different item that goes with the purchase
A correct example of cross-selling
Both should help the guest, with no pressure

essays.stem: Explain why product knowledge is important when you promote products, and describe how you would learn about your property's products and services.
essays.modelAnswer: Guests trust staff who can answer their questions quickly and correctly. If I know the products, prices, opening times and what is included in each package, I can suggest the right thing for each guest, explain the benefits and avoid giving wrong information that leads to complaints. To learn, I read the menus, brochures, package details and price lists, and I check them each day for changes and specials. I taste the dishes and drinks when the property allows, so I can describe them well. I visit the spa, the rooms, the pool and other areas so I can describe them. I ask the chef about ingredients and allergens, and I ask my supervisor and the tour desk about tours, transport and local attractions run by licensed operators. I attend training such as Team Jamaica.
markingPoints: Allows correct answers and builds guest trust
Helps match the right product to each guest and explain benefits
Avoids wrong information and complaints
Learns from menus, brochures, price lists and daily updates
Tastes, visits, asks the chef, supervisor and tour desk, and attends training

essays.stem: Describe how you find out a guest's needs before you suggest a product or service.
essays.modelAnswer: I start by greeting the guest warmly and giving them my full attention. I watch for clues, such as whether they are a family with children, a couple, a business guest or a large group, or whether they look tired after a flight. I ask open questions that cannot be answered with just yes or no, for example, "What would you like to do while you are in Jamaica?" or "What kind of food do you enjoy?" I listen carefully to the answers, without interrupting, and I nod and repeat key points to show I understand. I check the guest's booking for notes, such as a birthday or a special diet, but I keep private details private. Then I match one or two suitable products to what they have told me and explain how each would help them.
markingPoints: Greets warmly and gives full attention
Watches for clues about the type of guest
Asks open questions
Listens carefully and checks understanding
Uses booking notes privately and matches products to the needs

essays.stem: Describe how you would offer a room upgrade to a guest at check-in.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the system to see which better rooms are free and what the extra charge is, as the property's rates say. While I check the guest in, I make friendly conversation and listen for clues, such as a honeymoon, a birthday or a long stay. At the right moment, before I hand over the key, I describe the better room by its benefits, for example, "For a small extra charge each night, I can give you a room with its own balcony facing the sea, where you can enjoy the sunrise." I tell the guest the exact extra cost and whether GCT is included. If the guest agrees, I change the booking, record the upgrade and get their signature. If they say no, I thank them politely and carry on with the check-in, without asking again.
markingPoints: Checks availability and the correct extra charge first
Listens for clues such as a special occasion
Offers at the right time, before the key is given
Describes the benefits and gives the exact price clearly
Records and gets agreement, or accepts a no politely

essays.stem: Describe how a server can promote and up-sell during a meal, from seating the guests to presenting the bill.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guests are seated, the server welcomes them and suggests drinks, for example a fresh fruit punch, a sorrel or a cocktail, offering a choice of two. When presenting the menu, the server mentions the chef's specials and describes them in an appetising way, such as "pan-fried snapper with escovitch sauce". When taking the order, the server suggests a starter, a side dish such as festival or bammy, or a larger size, and checks for allergies. During the meal, the server checks that the guests are happy and offers another drink when glasses are nearly empty. When the plates are cleared, the server shows the dessert menu and suggests something like a slice of rum cake or sweet potato pudding with coffee. The server never pushes, and presents a clear, correct bill at the end.
markingPoints: Suggests drinks on seating, offering a choice
Describes specials in an appetising way
Suggests starters, sides or larger sizes and checks allergies
Offers more drinks and dessert at the right time
No pressure; presents a clear, correct bill

essays.stem: Explain the rules a staff member should follow to promote and sell responsibly.
essays.modelAnswer: I am honest about every product: I give the correct price, say whether GCT is included and describe things as they really are, so guests are not misled. I never promise something the property cannot deliver. I do not pressure guests; I suggest once or twice at the right time and accept "no" politely. I check allergens and special diets with the kitchen before suggesting food, and never guess. I do not sell alcohol to anyone under 18, and I ask for ID if a guest looks young. I do not serve more alcohol to a guest who is clearly drunk, and I offer water or a soft drink instead. I recommend only tours and services from licensed, safe operators. I follow the property's rules for social media and guest privacy when promoting products.
markingPoints: Honest prices and descriptions, including GCT
No pressure; accepts no
Checks allergens and diets with the kitchen
Responsible alcohol sales: no under-18s, ask for ID, no service to drunk guests
Recommends licensed operators and follows social media and privacy rules

essays.stem: A guest says "I'll think about it" when you suggest a spa package. Explain how to deal with a guest's doubts politely.
essays.modelAnswer: I stay friendly and do not push. I ask a gentle open question to find out what is worrying the guest, for example, "Is there anything I can tell you about the package?" I listen carefully. If the worry is the price, I can explain what is included and the benefits, or suggest a shorter or smaller treatment that costs less. If the worry is time, I can suggest a booking at a time that suits them, or tell them the spa's opening hours. If they worry about something like an allergy or a health condition, I suggest they speak to the spa therapist first. I give them a brochure or the details to take away, so they can decide later. If they still say no, I thank them and accept their answer, and leave the door open for them to come back.
markingPoints: Stays friendly and does not push
Asks an open question and listens to find the real worry
Answers the worry: explains benefits or offers a smaller or cheaper option
Offers another time or a brochure to take away
Accepts a no politely and leaves the offer open

essays.stem: Describe how to plan and make a poster or table tent to promote one product at a property.
essays.modelAnswer: First I find out what the product is, who it is for and when it is on, and I check the details and prices with my supervisor. I decide what guests most need to know: the name of the product, the main benefit, the day and time, the place, the price and whether GCT is included. I write a short, catchy heading and only a few clear lines, with large, easy-to-read letters. I use a picture or photo of the product, taken with permission, and the property's colours and logo as its rules say. I check the spelling and the facts carefully before printing. I get the design approved, then place the posters or table tents where the right guests will see them, such as the lobby, the bar or the restaurant tables. I remove them when the offer ends.
markingPoints: Finds out and checks the product details and prices
Includes the key facts: what, when, where, price and GCT
Short heading, clear large text and a suitable picture
Checks spelling and facts and gets approval
Places it where the right guests will see it and removes it when the offer ends

essays.stem: Explain how staff in different departments can work together to promote the property's products, and why sales are recorded.
essays.modelAnswer: Every department can help sell the others. The front desk can tell arriving guests about the restaurant's jerk night and the spa. Housekeeping can leave a card about a special in the room and pass on requests they hear. Servers can mention the tour desk, and the bar can promote the Sunday brunch. When a staff member hears about a birthday, an anniversary or a special need, they pass it on so the right team can offer something suitable. Staff share information about specials at the daily briefing. Sales are recorded so the property can see which promotions work and which do not, plan stock and staffing, give feedback to staff and, in some places, reward staff who reach their targets. Records also help the property improve its offers using guest feedback.
markingPoints: Each department can promote other departments' products (an example)
Passes on guest information such as special occasions
Shares information about specials at briefings
Sales records show which promotions work and help planning
Records give feedback, rewards for targets and help improve offers

essays.stem: Explain why promoting Jamaican products and experiences helps the guest, the property and the community. Give examples.
essays.modelAnswer: Visitors come to Jamaica to enjoy its culture, food and natural beauty. When I suggest local products, such as ackee and saltfish for breakfast, jerk chicken with festival, Blue Mountain coffee, a slice of rum cake or a bottle of local hot pepper sauce, the guest gets a real taste of Jamaica and a more memorable stay. Suggesting tours run by licensed operators, such as a river trip, a visit to a waterfall or a coffee farm, gives them safe and interesting experiences. The property gains extra sales and good reviews, and guests are more likely to come back. The community gains because money goes to local farmers, craft makers, tour guides and suppliers, which supports jobs. Promoting Jamaican products also helps protect and share our culture with the world.
markingPoints: Gives the guest a real and memorable Jamaican experience
Suitable examples of local food, drink, crafts or tours
Recommends licensed operators for safety
The property gains sales, good reviews and repeat guests
The community gains jobs and income, and culture is shared

practical1.title: Role play: promote and up-sell at the front desk and in the restaurant
practical1.brief: Set up a mock front desk and a mock restaurant table with menus, a drinks list, a dessert menu, brochures and price lists for rooms, the spa and tours (prepared by the Centre, with made-up prices and GCT shown "at the current rate"). Each member, in turn, does two short role plays from scenario cards: one at the front desk (for example, a honeymoon couple checking in, a family asking about things to do, a business guest) and one at the table (taking an order and suggesting drinks, sides and dessert). In each role play, the member greets the guest, finds out their needs with open questions, suggests one or two suitable products by their benefits, gives the correct price, deals with one doubt or "no", and records the result on a sales log. The other members play guests and observers, and each observer fills in a short peer feedback sheet. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, the sales logs and the feedback sheets to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: A mock front desk and a laid restaurant table
Menus, a drinks list, a dessert menu, brochures and price lists made up by the Centre
Scenario cards for each member, with made-up guest names and needs
Sales log sheets and peer feedback sheets
Pens, a clipboard and a phone or camera for photos
photos: The front desk and table set up with the promotional materials
A member greeting a "guest" and asking an open question
A member showing a brochure or menu while describing a benefit
A member suggesting dessert after the main course is cleared
A member dealing with a doubt or a "no"
The completed sales logs and peer feedback sheets
checklist: Greeted the guest warmly with good body language
Used open questions and listened to find the guest's needs
Suggested suitable products and described their benefits
Gave the correct price and said whether GCT is included
Offered at the right time, without pressure
Dealt with a doubt politely and accepted a "no"
Checked allergens or age where food or alcohol was suggested
Recorded the result correctly on the sales log
safety: Use only made-up guest names and details
Keep the floor around the desk and table clear so nobody trips
In role plays, keep a polite distance and do not touch the "guest"
No real alcohol: use empty bottles or pictures if drinks are shown

practical2.title: Plan, make and present a promotion for one property product
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group one product to promote, for example a Sunday Jamaican brunch, a spa afternoon for couples or a sunset cruise run by a licensed operator, with made-up details and prices. As a group, plan the promotion on a planning sheet: who it is for, the main benefits, the price (with GCT "at the current rate" as the assessor gives it), when and where it will be promoted. Each member makes one part: a poster, a table tent card, a short social media post (on paper or a screen, following the Centre's rules), a selling script for staff, or a sales record sheet. Then each member presents their part to the assessor and uses the script to promote the product to a "guest" in a short role play. Photograph each stage below and add the photos, the planning sheet and each member's piece to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: The product details and prices from the assessor
Card, paper, coloured pens, rulers and glue, or a computer and printer
Pictures of the product (made by the group or from the Centre)
photos: The group planning the promotion, with the planning sheet
The table tent card standing on a table
The social media post, on paper or on screen
The selling script and the sales record sheet
A member presenting and role-playing the promotion with a "guest"
checklist: Took part in planning: who it is for, benefits, price, when and where
Made their piece with correct, true details and price, including GCT
Used clear, short wording that is easy to read
Checked spelling and facts before the piece was finished
Followed the Centre's rules on social media and photos
Presented their piece clearly to the assessor
Promoted the product to a "guest" with benefits and no pressure
safety: Use scissors carefully and pass them handles first
Use only photos the group has permission to use; no guests' faces
Keep cables from the computer and printer tidy
